title: A budget-aware memory counts the notes of the memory it wraps: they reach the model whole, and the history makes room for them, keeping fewer events than the same window keeps without them
notes: Two agents with the same window of 520 tokens (min_events 1) read the same conversation; the second's scripted memory retrieves a note of about 40 tokens (len // 4 + 1, as Python's BudgetAwareMemory estimates) for every turn. Without the note the second turn keeps the first question and the third the first answer, the second question and its answer (memory/a-budget-keeps-the-latest-events-that-fit); with it each turn's history drops the oldest question, which no longer fits, and the note is not trimmed.
